module: Swaps Forest objects (theForest) on the fly with real physical "prop" vehicles (e.g. street lamp, trash bin) when the player gets close, so they can be hit and deformed. A pool of deactivated vehicles is created; every frame, the forest slots closest to the player (within spawnInViewRange) receive a vehicle from the pool and the forest object is moved under the map (z = -999); slots that are too far are given back to the forest. Experimental module: it contains debugging dump() calls.
usage:
extensions.load('core_dynamicProps')
core_dynamicProps.createDynamicProps({forestItemName = 'postbox_blue', propName = 'trashbin', poolSize = 9, spawnInViewRange = 150, spawnOffset = vec3(0,0,0)})
-- ... later
core_dynamicProps.unloadAll()
notes: Parameters of createDynamicProps: name (default "DynamicPropsId<n>"), forestItemName (name of the forest data to replace), propName (vehicle model to spawn), poolSize (default 10), spawnInViewRange in meters (default 100), spawnOffset vec3 (default 0,0,0), artifacts (table, unused).
onUpdate assumes player 0 has a vehicle (getPlayerVehicle(0):getPosition()) and that core_camera exists; without a player vehicle, Lua error.

Bugs/inconsistencies: unloadAll sets tempCopy = deepcopy(...) then DynamicProps:unload does tempCopy[self] = nil (an object key that does not exist in a list); calling unload() after deepcopy rebuilds dynamicPropsObjs from that copy, so the state is not really cleared. spawnProp/despawnProp call dump("Spawning"/"Despawning") on every switch. checkVisibility (local, unused) is full of dump().
Props are vehicles: they appear in the vehicle lists and are named <propName><i> (with identical licenseText).

createDynamicProps.desc: Creates a dynamic props manager: indexes the forest objects named forestItemName in a quadtree, spawns poolSize deactivated vehicles (setActive(0)), reloads collision (be:reloadCollision) and adds it to the list updated by onUpdate.

data.desc: forestItemName, propName, poolSize, spawnInViewRange, spawnOffset, name, artifacts (see notes). An empty table is rejected (error log, no object created).

onUpdate.desc: Per-frame hook: stores the camera and player 0 positions, then updates each manager (swaps forest objects <-> props).

unloadAll.desc: Puts all swapped forest objects back in place, deletes the pool's prop vehicles and reloads collision (see notes on the retained state).

westCoastPole.desc: Preset for West Coast USA: replaces "pole_city1" with the "streetlight" vehicle (pool 1, range 100 m, z offset -0.22).

westCoastBin.desc: Preset for West Coast USA: replaces "postbox_blue" with the "trashbin" vehicle (pool 9, range 150 m).

DynamicProps.desc: A dynamic props manager (pool) for one forest object type. Fields: name, forestItemName, propName, poolSize, spawnInViewRange, spawnOffset, props (table<vehId, boolean>: true = used), locationsInfo (list of locations {forestItem, switched, originPos, distance, linkedPropId, id}), forestQt (quadtree).

new.desc: Constructor; returns nil (error log) if data is empty.

__tostring.desc: Text "Pool name : ... Forest item : ... Prop Item : ...".

spawnProps.desc: Spawns poolSize propName vehicles (named propName..i, deactivated, without entering them) and marks them free.

findForestItems.desc: Looks up the "theForest" object, lists its items whose data name equals forestItemName and builds the locations quadtree (logs if there is no forest).

getFirstPropAvailable.desc: Takes the first free vehicle of the pool and marks it used.

returns.desc: vehicle id, nil if the pool is exhausted

spawnProp.desc: Hides the forest object (moves it under the map), activates the vehicle and places it at the origin position + spawnOffset with the forest object's rotation.

despawnProp.desc: Resets the vehicle to new condition (resetBrokenFlexMesh), deactivates it and puts the forest object back at its original position.

onUpdate.desc: Selects the locations within the player's range, sorts them by distance, gives back to the forest those that leave the range or exceed the pool, and gives a vehicle to the closest ones.

unload.desc: Gives back all swapped locations then deletes the pool's vehicles (also removes from the editor if present).
